direction() persists s3ShapeDir during a moving but invisible frame. Deferring it until visibility changes the heading when that projectile stops before reappearing. The actual direction function regression produces [0,1,0] with original updates versus [1,0,0] when the hidden update is skipped. Preserving history requires the same normalized direction work, eliminating the proposed low-risk saving.

Reuses per-seed phase sine/cosine and one age sine/cosine after two eligible warm-up frames. A conservative Float32 rounding-boundary check reruns the original sine when needed. More than 100 seeds across 30/60/120 Hz, capacity/culling, seed reuse and nonfinite/large-angle cases retain every finite Float32 output and signed zero. A warmed 300-frame operation-count regression reduces phase trig calls from 8400 to 654 with zero finite Float32 differences; no wall-clock/FPS claim is made.
